title: A Parrot Once Asked, 'What Color?' Looking in a Mirror
subject: african grey parrot

scenes.text: A parrot once looked in a mirror and asked a question.
Alex, an African grey parrot, studied his reflection and asked, what color? He then learned the word gray.
He knew the words for one through six, and in 2003 and 2004 he answered questions like what color six correctly over 80 percent of the time.
Then, asked what color five about a tray with no five, he said none. He'd only been trained to use none for same and different.
Researchers called it a zero-like concept he applied on his own.
Alex died in 2007 at about 31. His last words were: you be good, see you tomorrow. I love you.

description:
Alex the African grey parrot asked what color he was when he saw his reflection.
He also used the word none for a missing quantity, a zero-like idea nobody trained him to use.
What do you think he understood?
